text: I was hurt in a car accident in Adelaide. Which compensation lawyers should I contact?

result.keyword: I was hurt in a car accident in Adelaide. Which compensation lawyers should I contact?
result.markdown:
I’m sorry you’ve been hurt. In Adelaide, a car-accident injury will generally involve a **South Australian CTP (compulsory third-party) claim**, assuming another party was at least partly responsible. You can claim for things such as medical treatment, lost income, pain and suffering, and care/support, depending on the circumstances. [www.ctp.sa.gov.au](https://www.ctp.sa.gov.au/for-injured-people/who-can-claim?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### Adelaide lawyers I’d shortlist

These firms have a specific personal-injury focus and Adelaide offices:

- BTD Lawyers — Adelaide CBD; particularly worth considering for a specialist personal-injury practice.
- MKF Personal Injury Lawyers Adelaide — King William St; personal-injury specialist.
- PMN Personal Injury Lawyers Adelaide — Grenfell St; personal-injury specialist.
- DBH Lawyers — Wright St; established personal-injury practice.
- Turner Freeman Lawyers — Waymouth St; established national personal-injury firm.
- Johnston Withers Lawyers — Sturt St; Adelaide firm with personal-injury experience.
- Andersons Solicitors — Franklin St; personal-injury practice.
- Tindall Gask Bentley, Adelaide — Light Square; established Adelaide law firm.

I wouldn't choose purely on Google ratings. **Ask each lawyer specifically about SA CTP claims, their experience with injuries like yours, and the total likely legal cost.** The SA CTP Regulator specifically recommends discussing what the lawyer will do, how they charge, additional costs and an estimate of total legal costs before engaging them. [www.ctp.sa.gov.au](https://www.ctp.sa.gov.au/for-injured-people/legal-advice?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### One important deadline

If the crash was **less than three years ago**, you will generally still be within the SA CTP claim period, but you should start promptly. If it's been more than six months, the insurer will ask for an explanation for the delay; after three years, claims are generally not accepted except in limited circumstances. [ctp.sa.gov.au](https://ctp.sa.gov.au/for-injured-people/frequently-asked-questions?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[ctp.sa.gov.au](https://ctp.sa.gov.au/for-injured-people/lodge-your-claim?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

You also **don't have to wait for a lawyer before lodging a CTP claim**. [ctp.sa.gov.au](https://ctp.sa.gov.au/for-injured-people/frequently-asked-questions?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[ctp.sa.gov.au](https://ctp.sa.gov.au/for-injured-people/lodge-your-claim?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If you tell me **(1) when the accident happened, (2) whether you were the driver/passenger/pedestrian, and (3) roughly what injuries you suffered**, I can narrow this down to **3 Adelaide firms I'd contact first**, including which ones appear best suited to your type of claim and what questions to ask at the first consultation.
